note: Who can reach a given source of personal data, and how. Openness is a property of the platform, not of any one agent: an agent's own record says which path it takes.

items.label: Gmail
items.note: A full API exists, but restricted scopes require Google verification and an annual CASA security assessment.

items.label: Google Drive & Docs
items.note: Open to third parties through restricted scopes, subject to verification and annual assessment.

items.label: Google Calendar
items.note: Available to third parties through the standard Google Calendar API.

items.label: Google Photos library
items.note: Google removed the photoslibrary scopes after March 2025, leaving third parties a picker only, then shipped Gemini reading Photos directly. The clearest case of a door being closed and then walked through.

items.label: Outlook, Teams & OneDrive
items.note: Microsoft Graph and Copilot connectors give third parties close to the same reach as Copilot itself, with admin consent. The most open major stack.

items.label: X public posts
items.note: Purchasable rather than exclusive: xAI sells an X Search tool and X sells an enterprise firehose advertising 100% of public posts. Nothing documents Grok receiving data its API customers cannot buy.

items.label: X direct messages
items.note: Readable through the X API on a per-message charge. No first-party agent access is documented either.

items.label: Instagram & Facebook profile
items.note: Meta's assistant reaches profile and engagement data through Accounts Center. No equivalent third-party API exists for a personal Instagram or Facebook graph.

items.label: Instagram direct messages
items.note: The Instagram API covers professional accounts only, and Meta states its own generative AI excludes private messages. Closed to third parties and to Meta's assistant alike.

items.label: WhatsApp messages
items.note: End-to-end encrypted. WhatsApp states personal messages are not seen by Meta AI, and Private Processing is built so that Meta cannot decrypt requests. Unreachable by anyone, including its owner.

items.label: iMessage
items.note: The hardest lock in this table. Apple's Messages framework covers composing and stickers; there is no read path, while Siri's on-device index reads message content.

items.label: WeChat messages
items.note: No personal-messaging API exists on the WeChat open platform, for third parties or for Tencent's own assistant.

items.label: Feishu / Lark
items.note: Message history, documents, calendar and tasks are available to third parties through published Lark scopes, the same access the first-party assistant uses.

items.label: Apple Health
items.note: Open to third parties through HealthKit with the person's consent. Siri's advantage here is convenience, not exclusivity.

items.label: Apple Photos
items.note: Open to third parties through PhotoKit with consent.

items.label: Windows screen history
items.note: Recall snapshots the screen locally and exposes no API, so only Microsoft's own assistant can use it.

items.label: Amazon purchases & viewing
items.note: Alexa+ reads what you bought, listened to and watched. There is no consumer order API, so outside the EU third parties have nothing; inside it, DMA portability scopes cover orders, Fire TV and Kindle.

items.label: TikTok
items.note: No general API, but the EU and UK Data Portability API ships direct messages — a case where regulation gives third parties more than the platform otherwise would.

items.label: LinkedIn
items.note: Member data portability under the DMA gives authorised third parties recurring access in the EU.
